findings.title: join() breaks out early leaving remaining processes un-terminated
findings.body: When the deadline expires partway through the loop, `break` skips `process.terminate()` for all remaining processes. Those flusher processes keep running and keep producing after the consumer has shut down or rebalanced. Shards can then be flushed twice by the old and new owners. The loop should still terminate every process after the deadline passes.

findings.title: Zero assigned shards causes modulo/empty process map issues
findings.body: If a rebalance assigns no partitions, `assigned_shards` is empty and `num_processes` becomes 0. No flusher runs, and every per-process loop is a no-op. More importantly, `self.max_processes` is set from `max_processes or len(...)`, so passing 0 falls back silently. The previous single-process behaviour always ran a flusher. This needs at least a guard or an explicit decision about the zero-shard case.

findings.title: isinstance check against multiprocessing.Process misses SpawnProcess
findings.body: Processes are created from the spawn context (`SpawnProcess`), which is a subclass of `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`. As a result, `kill()` in `_ensure_processes_alive` is never called on hung processes. The same applies to `terminate()` in `join()`. A hung flusher is therefore left running alongside its replacement, and both flush the same shards. Check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` instead.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name 'shards' vs 'shard'
findings.body: The `wait_produce` timer uses the tag key `shards`, while the other flusher metrics use `shard`. This breaks dashboards and queries that filter by a single key.
